feature: Set the position and size of several layers at once
summary: The Position & Size fields now speak for everything you have picked, not just the last layer you clicked. Select a row of buttons, type one width, and they all take it in a single undo step.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Experiments flag "Type a layer's position and size" is on by default. Start a blank canvas (File > New) and draw three rectangles of different widths at different left edges.

try.do: With the Select tool, drag a rubber band around all three rectangles.
Read the Position & Size section: X, Y and W should say Mixed, H should say 60.
Press Command Z once, and check all three widths come back at the same time.
Redo, then click X, type 100 and press Return, so every left edge lines up.
Click Y (still Mixed) and press the up arrow, then Shift and up arrow.
Draw an arrow, rubber band all four layers, and hover the W field.
Type 120 into W and press Return: the three rectangles resize, the arrow does not.

evaluate: When the fields say Mixed, is it obvious that typing a number will change every picked layer rather than just one?
Typing an X moves every layer onto that left edge. Is that what you expected, or did you expect the whole group to slide across as one block?
Pressing up arrow on a Mixed field moves everything by 1 but the field still reads Mixed. Does that feel right or does it look like nothing happened?
The caption under the fields runs three lines. Is it earning its space, or is it noise once you have used the section twice?
With an arrow in the selection, W shows 160 for the three rectangles that have a width. Is a number that speaks for part of the selection honest enough, or should it say Mixed?
rough: The fact that W only reaches 3 of 4 picked layers lives in the hover tip alone. Nothing on the field itself hints that one layer is sitting out.
An arrow key on a Mixed field is the one edit with no visible change in the panel: the layers move on canvas but the box still reads Mixed.
Dragging several layers on canvas does not update the fields live the way a single-layer drag does. The numbers catch up on mouse up.

Typing X sets every layer's own left edge rather than moving the selection's bounding box. The task notes flagged this as a possible decision card, but the acceptance list had already settled it, and it is the only reading that makes "lines every selected layer up on that edge" true.
Verified live: the probe held Screen Recording, so all three shots are real window captures from Scripts/playtest/multi-geometry-walk.json.
